keywords.def: meaningless noises and sounds which babies make as they start learning to speak
sound within a word which is emphasised by being spoken longer, louder or higher than the other sounds
perfect or most typical example of something which has all the features which you expect such a thing to have
accept or assume something without question
having more than one possible meaning; being open to interpretation

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: This is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 这是来自 BBC 学习英语的 6 Minute English。

sentences.en: I’m Phil. And I’m Georgie. For most parents, their baby’s first word is a special moment.
sentences.zh: 我是 Phil。我是 Georgie。对大多数父母来说，宝宝的第一个词是一个特别的时刻。

sentences.en: This happens after an early stage of language development called babble, when babies start making simple sounds like "ga" or "ma".
sentences.zh: 这发生在被称为咿呀学语的早期语言发展阶段之后，当时宝宝开始发出诸如"ga"或"ma"之类的简单声音。

sentences.en: Babies have to learn to use their mouth muscles to make specific sounds.
sentences.zh: 宝宝必须学会使用他们的口腔肌肉来发出特定的声音。

sentences.en: They experiment with different sounds and mouth shapes.
sentences.zh: 他们用不同的声音和嘴型做实验。

sentences.en: So, what exactly is happening when babies start learning to speak?
sentences.zh: 那么，当宝宝开始学说话时，究竟发生了什么？

sentences.en: What do you think, Georgie? Well, Phil, I'm no expert, but I imagine they watch the adults around them and kind of copy and imitate what they do.
sentences.zh: 你觉得呢，Georgie？嗯，Phil，我不是专家，但我猜他们会观察周围的成年人，并且有点像模仿他们所做的事情。

sentences.en: What do you think? I definitely think that's what my children did when they were learning to speak.
sentences.zh: 你觉得呢？我绝对认为我的孩子在学说话时就是这样的。

sentences.en: Well, let’s compare our ideas with those of an expert - Professor Julian Pine from Liverpool University, speaking here on BBC Radio 4, and he lists the skills that babies develop in order to speak:
sentences.zh: 好吧，让我们把我们的想法与专家——来自利物浦大学的 Julian Pine 教授的想法进行对比，他在 BBC Radio 4 的节目中发言，他列出了宝宝为了说话而发展的技能：

sentences.en: Well, one of the first things the child's got to do is, they've got to break down the speech stream into words.
sentences.zh: 嗯，孩子要做的第一件事之一，就是他们必须把语音流分解成单词。

sentences.en: Then they've got to link the words to the things that they refer to in the environment, so they've got to learn what the words mean. [Right].
sentences.zh: 然后他们必须把这些单词和它们在环境中指代的事物联系起来，所以他们必须了解这些词的意思。[对的。]

sentences.en: In this programme, we’ll discover how babies learn to speak, and, as usual, we’ll learn some useful new vocabulary.
sentences.zh: 在本期节目中，我们将探讨宝宝是如何学会说话的，并且像往常一样，我们将学习一些有用的新词汇。

sentences.en: And on the subject of words, remember you can find a list of this programme’s vocabulary on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 说到单词，请记住你可以在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上找到本期节目的词汇列表。

sentences.en: Some people find it helpful to study the vocabulary before listening.
sentences.zh: 有些人发现在听之前学习这些词汇很有帮助。

sentences.en: And another thing to do before listening is ask my question, Georgie.
sentences.zh: 在听之前要做的另一件事是问我的问题，Georgie。

sentences.en: We’ve mentioned the babbling noises that babies make when learning to speak, but at what age does this usually start?
sentences.zh: 我们提到了宝宝在学说话时发出的咿呀学语的声音，但这通常在什么年龄开始？

sentences.en: Is it: a) around 6 months old? b) around 9 months old? or, c) around 1 year old?
sentences.zh: 是：a) 大约 6 个月大？b) 大约 9 个月大？还是 c) 大约 1 岁大？

sentences.en: OK, I think my best guess would be a) around six months old.
sentences.zh: 好的，我最好的猜测是 a) 大约六个月大。

sentences.en: OK, well, we'll find out a little bit later on in the programme.
sentences.zh: 好的，我们在节目稍后会揭晓。

sentences.en: Let’s return to Professor Pine’s list. The first thing babies do is recognise where individual words start and end.
sentences.zh: 让我们回到 Pine 教授的列表中。宝宝做的第一件事是识别单个单词的起点和终点。

sentences.en: For this it helps to know that, in English at least, words often begin with a stressed syllable – the sound in a word which is emphasised by being spoken longer or louder.
sentences.zh: 为此，了解这一点会有所帮助，至少在英语中，单词通常以重读音节开始——即通过说得更长或更大声而被强调的音节。

sentences.en: Learning this takes time, and here, Professor Pine and Michael Rosen, presenter of BBC Radio 4’s programme, 'Word of Mouth', discuss children who haven’t quite discovered it yet:
sentences.zh: 学习这个需要时间，在这里，Pine 教授和 BBC Radio 4 节目 "Word of Mouth" 的主持人 Michael Rosen 讨论了那些还没完全掌握这一点的孩子：

sentences.en: We can see this in the kind of errors that children make, because little kids will often call a giraffe a ‘raffe’ by leaving off the unstressed syllable because that's not typical English.
sentences.zh: 我们从孩子们犯的错误中可以看出这一点，因为小孩子经常把长颈鹿叫作‘raffe’，漏掉了非重读音节，因为那不是典型的英语。

sentences.en: Ooh, and I’ve got an example of this - my son used to call a machine a ‘sminge’ – he just hit the stress, he didn't bother with the ‘ma’ bit.
sentences.zh: 哦，我有一个这方面的例子——我儿子过去常常把机器叫作‘sminge’——他只抓住了重音，不费心去管‘ma’那个部分。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly. Or he may have thought it was ‘my sminge’ of course, that’s the other thing.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。或者他当然可能认为那是‘my sminge’，这是另一回事。

sentences.en: And the classic example, of course, is ‘nana’ instead of ‘banana’.
sentences.zh: 当然，经典的例子就是不用 ‘banana’ 而用 ‘nana’。

sentences.en: Yes, I think I call them that!
sentences.zh: 是的，我想我也这么叫它们！

sentences.en: One error, or mistake, infants make is calling a giraffe a ‘raffe’ because they cut off the first syllable 'gi' because it's not stressed.
sentences.zh: 婴儿犯的一个错误或失误是把长颈鹿叫作‘raffe’，因为他们切掉了第一个音节 ‘gi’，因为它没有被重读。

sentences.en: The classic example of this is when children say ‘nana’ instead of ‘banana’.
sentences.zh: 这方面的经典例子是孩子们说 ‘nana’ 而不是 ‘banana’。

sentences.en: A classic example of something means the best example of it, one containing all the features you expect such a thing to have.
sentences.zh: 某事物的经典例子意味着它是最好的例子，包含你期望这种事物具备的所有特征。

sentences.en: For example, ants are a classic example of animals working together.
sentences.zh: 例如，蚂蚁是动物协同工作的经典例子。

sentences.en: The second skill babies develop as they learn to speak is correctly linking a word to the object it refers to, in other words knowing what the word means.
sentences.zh: 宝宝在学说话时发展的第二项技能是将单词与它所指代的对象正确联系起来，换句话说，知道这个词的意思。

sentences.en: As adults we do this without thinking, but it’s actually much harder than it sounds, as Professor Julian Pine explains to BBC Radio 4 programme, 'Word of Mouth'.
sentences.zh: 作为成年人，我们不假思索地这样做听起来很简单，但实际上比听起来要难得多，正如 Julian Pine 教授向 BBC Radio 4 节目 "Word of Mouth" 解释的那样。

sentences.en: Well, we take for granted the fact that it's kind of obvious what words refer to in the environment, but actually if you look at it from the child's point of view, it's really difficult to work out what a word refers to because there's so many things it could refer to.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们认为理所当然的是，词语在环境中指代什么似乎是显而易见的，但实际上，如果你从孩子的角度来看，弄清楚一个词指的是什么真的很困难，因为它可能指代的东西太多了。

sentences.en: So, you know, the speech signal is very ambiguous.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，语音信号是非常含糊不清的。

sentences.en: How does the child know that you're talking about the cup in front of you, or the pen in front of you when you say ‘pen’ or ‘cup’?
sentences.zh: 孩子怎么知道当你说了‘pen’或‘cup’时，你谈论的是你面前的杯子，还是你面前的笔？

sentences.en: As adults, we take it for granted that when a friend says, “apple”, they mean that round, red thing on the table.
sentences.zh: 作为成年人，我们想当然地认为，当朋友说“苹果”时，他们指的是桌上那个圆圆的、红色的东西。

sentences.en: To take it for granted means to assume something without question.
sentences.zh: 认为某事理所当然意味着毫无疑问地接受某事。

sentences.en: But for a baby, the link between the word ‘apple’ and the object is not obvious, it’s ambiguous, meaning it has more than one possible meaning.
sentences.zh: 但对于婴儿来说，单词“apple”与物体之间的联系并不明显，它是含糊不清的，意味着它有一个以上可能的含义。

sentences.en: Wow! Who knew so much was going on inside babies’ sponge-like brains as they soak up the sounds they hear?
sentences.zh: 哇！谁知道当宝宝们吸收他们听到的声音时，他们海绵般的大脑里发生了这么多事情？

sentences.en: Right, Phil, isn’t it time to reveal the answer to your question?
sentences.zh: 对啦，Phil，是不是该揭晓你的问题答案了？

sentences.en: It is indeed. The question was, at what age do babies start to make babbling noises?
sentences.zh: 确实如此。问题是，宝宝在什么年龄开始发出咿呀学语的声音？

sentences.en: And I said it was around six months. And that is the correct answer.
sentences.zh: 我说大约六个月。这就是正确答案。

sentences.en: Yay! Babies start to do this when they're about 6 months old.
sentences.zh: 耶！宝宝在大约 6 个月大时开始这样做。

sentences.en: OK, let’s recap the vocabulary that we’ve learned starting with babble, the meaningless noises babies make as they’re learning to speak.
sentences.zh: 好的，让我们回顾一下我们学过的词汇，从 babble 开始，这是宝宝在学说话时发出的无意义的声音。

sentences.en: The stressed syllable in a word is the sound which is emphasised by being longer, louder, or higher.
sentences.zh: 单词中的重读音节是通过更长、更大声或更高而被强调的声音。

sentences.en: An error is a mistake. The classic example of something is the most typical example of it, containing its most important features.
sentences.zh: error 就是错误。某事物的经典例子是最典型的例子，包含了它最重要的特征。

sentences.en: If you take something for granted, you accept or assume it without question.
sentences.zh: 如果你把某事视为理所当然，你就会毫无疑问地接受或假设它。

sentences.en: And finally, the adjective ambiguous means having more than one possible meaning.
sentences.zh: 最后，形容词 ambiguous 意为具有一种以上的可能含义。

sentences.en: Once again, our six minutes are up, but if you’re ready for more you’ll find the worksheet with a quiz and a transcript for this programme on our website – see you there soon!
sentences.zh: 我们的六分钟又到了，但如果你准备好了解更多，你可以在我们的网站上找到本期节目的带有小测验和字幕的工作表——很快在那里见！

sentences.en: Bye! Bye!
sentences.zh: 拜拜！拜拜！
